title: Predictive factors of early progression after CAR T-cell therapy in relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Predictive factors of early progression after CAR T-cell therapy in relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-3】The purpose of our study was to identify factors that may predict failure, particularly early progression (EP), within the first month after infusion.

evidence.text: The purpose of our study was to identify factors that may predict failure, particularly early progression (EP), within the first month after infusion.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Predictive factors of early progression after CAR T-cell therapy in relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】Characteristics of 116 patients were analyzed at the time of decision (TD) to use commercial CAR (axicabtagene ciloleucel, n = 49; tisagenlecleucel n = 67) and at the time of treatment (TT), together with total metabolic tumor volume (TMTV) at TT.

【Abstract · abstract-1-5】With a median follow-up of 8.2 months, 55 patients failed treatment; 27 (49%) were early progressors.

evidence.text: Characteristics of 116 patients were analyzed at the time of decision (TD) to use commercial CAR (axicabtagene ciloleucel, n = 49; tisagenlecleucel n = 67) and at the time of treatment (TT), together with total metabolic tumor volume (TMTV) at TT.
With a median follow-up of 8.2 months, 55 patients failed treatment; 27 (49%) were early progressors.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Predictive factors of early progression after CAR T-cell therapy in relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-6】The estimated 12-month progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were 47.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 38.0-58.6) and 67.0% (95% CI, 57-79), respectively.

evidence.text: The estimated 12-month progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were 47.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 38.0-58.6) and 67.0% (95% CI, 57-79), respectively.
